title: Customer Rage Case File
oneLiner: A consumer counter-service tool that converts bad support loops, dynamic-pricing suspicion, and refund dead ends into a clean complaint packet.
label: Fun / Portfolio / Commercial
targetUser: Consumers stuck with airlines, telecoms, retailers, or subscription companies who feel exploited but need evidence instead of ranting.
keyUX: User drops receipts, support chats, screenshots, and timeline facts; the app turns anger into a calm complaint file, escalation target, and refund ask.

sourceSignals.source: The Guardian, 2026-06-24, Record profits, terrible service
sourceSignals.signal: U.S. consumers report record frustration with service quality, dynamic pricing, junk fees, and limited alternatives while complaint volume rises.
States and cities are pushing rules against junk fees and surveillance-based pricing as consumers suspect individualized pricing is becoming unfair.

spreadTrigger: The before/after case card is shareable because it turns a rant into a clean win attempt.
stitchPrompt: Build a production-grade web app prototype called "Customer Rage Case File" for consumers trapped in terrible support loops, suspicious dynamic pricing, or refund dead ends. The first screen must be a working complaint packet builder with rage-to-evidence intake, fee and price-change timeline, support transcript sorter, refund ask calculator, regulator/company escalation selector, complaint letter preview, and shareable calm case card. Use realistic sample data: airline fee jump, telecom chat loop, subscription cancellation screenshot, 16% complaint surge note, junk fee line item, and a customer trying not to sound unhinged. Design direction: use the playful-experimental profile with a bold case-file metaphor, memorable evidence stamps, strong but readable contrast, and one obvious workflow that converts anger into leverage. Do not make a marketing landing page; the first screen must be the working app.
